answer.title: Keep receiving after an update that cannot be applied, and tell the owner
answer.body:
## Why

### One update a receiver cannot apply ends its node's executor: every later update, and every other callback of the node, stops ([LucaKro/cognitive_robot_abstract_machine#84](https://github.com/LucaKro/cognitive_robot_abstract_machine/issues/84))

One update a receiver cannot apply ends its node's executor, so no update is applied any more and every other callback of the node stops too, such as Giskard's action server and TF publisher. The process keeps running with a world that silently stops changing.

### A synchronizer that defers or pauses incoming updates dies on an update building on an earlier one, which Giskard always does ([LucaKro/cognitive_robot_abstract_machine#85](https://github.com/LucaKro/cognitive_robot_abstract_machine/issues/85))

A synchronizer that defers or pauses incoming updates dies on an update that builds on an earlier one, such as spawning a tray and then putting a cup on it. Giskard always defers its updates, so it stops receiving the world as soon as a publisher sends such a pair.

### A world's own echo is deserialized before being dropped, so changing and then removing an entity ends its executor ([LucaKro/cognitive_robot_abstract_machine#86](https://github.com/LucaKro/cognitive_robot_abstract_machine/issues/86))

A world deserializes its own echo before dropping it, so changing an entity and then removing it raises on the echo of the change and ends the node's executor. This happens in a single process, with nobody else involved.

<details>
<summary>What changes, how it is tested, and what breaks</summary>

<!-- github-workflow:changes:start -->
## What changes

A synchronizer keeps receiving after an update it cannot apply. It no longer reads its own echo, and it buffers updates as received, so later updates can build on earlier ones.

- **Updates that cannot be applied no longer end the node's executor (LucaKro/cognitive_robot_abstract_machine#84), and the owner of the world is told.**
  - `subscription_callback` catches the domain errors (`DataclassException`) that building or applying a received update raises: an unknown entity or degree of freedom, an invalid world after applying, and so on.
  - It logs them, throttled, with the publisher and the update number, and marks that publisher as diverged.
  - The failure is kept as a `SynchronizerDivergedError`, with the original error as `raised_from`. It is raised once on the thread that owns the world, at its next `has_applied`, `apply_missed_messages` or `apply_missed_state_updates`, or through `raise_unreported_divergence()`. The owner decides what to do, for example abort a goal or fetch the world again.
  - `has_applied` never reports a diverged publisher as caught up again.
  - Programming errors (`TypeError` and the like), `KeyboardInterrupt` and `SystemExit` are not caught.
- **The own echo is dropped before it is read (LucaKro/cognitive_robot_abstract_machine#86).** A received message is now a `ReceivedMessage`. Its origin and stream position are read from the JSON; the rest stays JSON. The echo of the synchronizer's own messages is dropped on that metadata alone, so it can no longer fail on entities the world has since removed.
- **Deferred and paused updates are built only when applied (LucaKro/cognitive_robot_abstract_machine#85).**
  - `missed_messages` buffers `ReceivedMessage`s. Each one is built against the world (`ReceivedMessage.to_message`) when it is applied, so a buffered update may refer to what an earlier buffered one introduces.
  - `has_buffered_model_modification` and `apply_missed_state_updates` read from the JSON whether a message modifies the model.
  - An update that cannot be built now fails in `apply_missed_messages`, on the thread that owns the world, rather than on the executor.

## Tests

- New `test_ros/test_synchronizer_survives_bad_updates.py`:
  - an update the receiver cannot apply does not raise;
  - the receiver keeps applying afterwards;
  - it stops reporting itself caught up with a publisher it diverged from;
  - the owner is told, once, with the original error;
  - its own echo is ignored without being read;
  - deferred updates that build on each other are all applied.

  All seven fail on `main`.
- Two existing tests asserted the behaviour this PR changes and were adapted (approved):
  - `test_an_update_referencing_an_entity_this_world_never_received_says_so` now expects `SynchronizerDivergedError` on the owner's thread. It checks publisher, entity id and name on the `WorldUpdateReferencesUnknownEntityError` it was raised from.
  - `test_a_model_modification_republishes_the_whole_state` builds the buffered `ReceivedMessage` with `to_message(world=...)` before reading its state.
- Ran `test/semantic_digital_twin_test/test_ros` locally with ROS Jazzy; these tests and the new ones pass.

## Breaks

`api-break`:
- `WorldSynchronizer.missed_messages` holds `ReceivedMessage`s instead of `WorldUpdate`s.
- `Synchronizer._subscription_callback` receives a `ReceivedMessage`.
- A received update that cannot be applied is logged and raised later on the owner's thread as `SynchronizerDivergedError`, instead of being raised on the executor thread.


🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01HTLXeCNA1TNameGRXxSMDn
<!-- github-workflow:changes:end -->

</details>

nodes.body: uhh why do you have that variable here again?
i think we have a real type alias fro JSONData

**A reload never clears the divergence Giskard checks.**

This forgets the divergence on the `ModelReloadSynchronizer`, but divergences are recorded per synchronizer instance, and the one Giskard queries belongs to the `WorldSynchronizer`: `IncomingWorldUpdates.divergence_from` (`giskardpy/.../world_updates.py:94`) and `has_applied` both go through `self.world_synchronizer`. The reload synchronizer's own `_divergences` is practically always empty (a `LoadModel` hardly fails to deserialize), so this call does nothing. Outside the tests, nothing calls `forget_divergence_from` on a `WorldSynchronizer`.

Consequence: after one update of a client fails to apply in Giskard, `has_applied` stays `False` for that client forever, and every later goal that waits on one of its updates fails with `RequiredWorldUpdateNotAppliedError`. That error tells the user to reload the world, which does not help. Only a restart of Giskard recovers.

Suggestion: when a reload is applied, clear the divergence on the world synchronizer of the same world, e.g. let `IncomingWorldUpdates.apply_all` forget the divergence on `world_synchronizer` after `apply_pending_reload` applied one, or give `ModelReloadSynchronizer` a way to reach the `WorldSynchronizer` of its world. Note that the `LoadModel` publisher and the diverged `WorldUpdate` publisher are the same process but may not compare equal as `MetaData`, so the clearing may need to go by node/process rather than by the exact `MetaData`. Please add a test for this: diverge, reload, then `has_applied` / a goal succeeds again.

**Catching `KeyError` and `ValueError` here is broad.** `DataclassException` is clearly a failure to apply, but a plain `KeyError`/`ValueError` from a genuine programming error anywhere in `from_json` or `apply_message` is now turned into a throttled log line plus a divergence, instead of failing loudly. It also contradicts the description, which says programming errors are not caught.

Could the specific cases that motivated this (e.g. the non-numeric state in `test_update_whose_state_is_no_number_is_reported`) be raised as `DataclassException`s where they arise, so that only those are caught here? If that is not feasible, please at least log the traceback for these two so a real bug is still diagnosable.

**An update can be half-applied.** In `apply_message` the model part is applied before the state part. If `_apply_model` succeeds and `_apply_state` then raises (e.g. `StateUpdateContainsUnknownDegreesOfFreedomError`), the world keeps the model change but `record_applied` is never called for the message. The same holds within `_apply_model` if `modifications.apply` raises part-way. Previously that ended the executor; now the process keeps running with a partially applied update.

Marking the publisher as diverged is the right reaction, but it only helps once recovery actually works (see the comment on `apply_reload`). Please either say in the docstring of `_handle_reporting_divergence` / `SynchronizerDivergedError` that the world may hold part of the failed update, or check the state update against the world before applying the model, so that a combined update is applied entirely or not at all.

answer.body:
The approach is sound, and the three fixes (surviving bad updates, dropping the own echo unread, building buffered updates lazily) are what we need. I am requesting changes because of the first point below: once Giskard has diverged from a client, there is currently no way back short of restarting Giskard.

**Description is stale (since aac31ee).** The "What changes" section still describes the earlier design:
- "raised once on the thread that owns the world, at its next `has_applied`, `apply_missed_messages` or `apply_missed_state_updates`, or through `raise_unreported_divergence()`": `raise_unreported_divergence` no longer exists; divergences are now queried with `divergence_from` and cleared with `forget_divergence_from`.
- "catches the domain errors (`DataclassException`)" / "Programming errors (`TypeError` and the like) … are not caught": `KeyError` and `ValueError` are caught as well now.
- Tests: "the owner is told, once": `test_asking_for_a_divergence_does_not_consume_it` asserts the opposite.
- Breaks: the new public `divergence_from` / `forget_divergence_from` and Giskard's `RequiredWorldUpdateNotAppliedError` are not mentioned.

Details inline.
